answer.worked:
Multiply (2) by $2$:
$$10x+2y=14\qquad\text{(3)}$$
Subtract (1) from (3):
$$\begin{align*}(10x+2y)-(3x+2y)&=14-7\\7x&=7\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute $x=1$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}5(1)+y&=7\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=1,\ y=2$.

Multiply (2) by $5$:
$$15x+35y=225\qquad\text{(3)}$$
Subtract (1) from (3):
$$\begin{align*}(15x+35y)-(15x+2y)&=225-27\\33y&=198\\y&=6\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=6$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}3x+7(6)&=45\\3x+42&=45\\3x&=3\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=1,\ y=6$.

Multiply (1) by $2$ and (2) by $3$:
$$\begin{aligned}6x+10y&=44&&\text{(3)}\\6x+21y&=99&&\text{(4)}\end{aligned}$$
Subtract (3) from (4):
$$\begin{align*}(6x+21y)-(6x+10y)&=99-44\\11y&=55\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=5$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}3x+5(5)&=22\\3x+25&=22\\3x&=-3\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=-1,\ y=5$.

content.prompt: A rectangular prism has width $y$ cm, length $(x+a)$ cm and height $(x+b)$ cm, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $a>b$.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the surface area of the rectangular prism is given by the expression
$$2y(2x+a+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\text{ cm}^2.$$

answer.worked:
The prism has three pairs of equal rectangular faces.
$$\begin{align*}S&=2y(x+a)+2y(x+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\\&=2y\bigl[(x+a)+(x+b)\bigr]+2(x+a)(x+b)\\&=2y(2x+a+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
If the surface area of the rectangular prism is equivalent to the expression
$$2y(2x+1)+2x^2+2x-12\text{ cm}^2,$$
find $a$ and $b$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}S&=2y(2x+a+b)+2\bigl[x^2+(a+b)x+ab\bigr]\\&=4xy+2(a+b)y+2x^2+2(a+b)x+2ab.\end{align*}$$
Equating the coefficients of $y$ and the constant terms gives
$$\begin{align*}2(a+b)&=2\\a+b&=1\\2ab&=-12\\ab&=-6.\end{align*}$$
The integers $3$ and $-2$ have sum $1$ and product $-6$. Since $a>b$, $a=3$ and $b=-2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the values of $k$ for which $x^2+8x+k=0$ has no real solutions.

answer.worked:
$a=1,\ b=8,\ c=k$.

$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=8^2-4(1)(k)\\&=64-4k\end{aligned}$$

For no real solutions, $\Delta<0$.

$$\begin{aligned}64-4k&<0\\-4k&<-64\\k&>16\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the values of $k$ for which $x^2+k=10x$ has two real solutions.

answer.worked:
$$x^2-10x+k=0$$

$a=1,\ b=-10,\ c=k$.

$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=(-10)^2-4(1)(k)\\&=100-4k\end{aligned}$$

For two real solutions, $\Delta>0$.

$$\begin{aligned}100-4k&>0\\-4k&>-100\\k&<25\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the values of $k$ for which $2x^2+4x+k=0$ has exactly one real solution.

answer.worked:
$a=2,\ b=4,\ c=k$.

$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=4^2-4(2)(k)\\&=16-8k\end{aligned}$$

For exactly one real solution, $\Delta=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}16-8k&=0\\8k&=16\\k&=2\end{aligned}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $x^{2}+2kx+(k^{2}-1)=0$ always has rational solutions for all rational $k$.

answer.short: $\Delta=4$, so the solutions $x=-k\pm1$ are rational for all rational $k$.
answer.worked:
$a=1$, $b=2k$, $c=k^{2}-1$.
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(2k)^{2}-4(1)(k^{2}-1)\\\Delta&=4k^{2}-4k^{2}+4\\\Delta&=4\end{align*}$$
Since $\sqrt{\Delta}=2$, the quadratic formula gives
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-2k\pm2}{2}\\x&=-k\pm1.\end{align*}$$
Both solutions are rational for all rational $k$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $x^{2}+(k+2)x+(k+1)=0$ always has rational solutions for all rational $k$.

answer.short: $\Delta=k^{2}$, so the solutions $-1$ and $-(k+1)$ are rational for all rational $k$.
answer.worked:
$a=1$, $b=k+2$, $c=k+1$.
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(k+2)^{2}-4(1)(k+1)\\\Delta&=k^{2}+4k+4-4k-4\\\Delta&=k^{2}\end{align*}$$
For rational $k$, $\sqrt{\Delta}=|k|$ is rational. The quadratic formula gives
$$x=\frac{-(k+2)\pm|k|}{2}.$$
The solutions are $-1$ and $-(k+1)$, both rational for all rational $k$. They are equal when $k=0$.
